title: When the Colony Turns
premise: Freya Galloway, the fourth clone of murdered transit-surveyor Elena Galloway, runs cargo along the Meridian Route between two human colonies that severed contact a decade ago. When the deep-space vessel Halcyon Dawn returns with its crew mysteriously aged backward, both colonies race to claim its cryo-banks—which hold the only viable genetic templates capable of restarting their failing populations. Freya discovers the ship's reversal was caused by her original's secret research, meaning Elena was murdered to keep it buried, and the killer now sits on the colonial council that raised Freya. In the end, Freya broadcasts Elena's findings to both worlds, forcing a shared custody of the Halcyon Dawn, and chooses her own identity over the legacy she was cloned to continue.
about_author: Noor Villalobos is a former maritime radio operator who spent nine years relaying messages between ships that rarely saw each other, an experience that shapes her fiction's obsession with distance and duty. She writes from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage, where she claims the fog does half her plotting.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She runs a solo cargo run between the colonies of Verdance and Kestrel's Reach, navigating the silence between two worlds that refuse to speak. Through her routine and her habit of recording messages she never sends, we learn she is a clone who inherited her original's unsolved murder. Emotional beat: competent loneliness masking a hunger to belong.

chapters.title: Inherited Ghosts
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At Verdance dock, councilman Aldous Wren greets her with unsettling familiarity—everyone treats her as Elena continued. She visits the archive of Elena's sealed case files and finds a page torn out. Emotional beat: the suffocating weight of living as someone else's unfinished story.

chapters.title: Signal from the Dark
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, with a Kestrel Reach dispatcher's interlude. A distress ping from deep space: the Halcyon Dawn, lost forty years ago, is returning. Both colonies scramble; the route that no longer speaks suddenly needs a courier. Emotional beat: the thrill of being needed cracking open old isolation.

chapters.title: The Ship That Forgot Its Age
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She rendezvous with the Halcyon Dawn and boards to find the crew biologically reversed to childhood—bodies of ten-year-olds with fragmented adult memories. A girl with an old woman's eyes begs her not to tell the councils everything. Emotional beat: horror braided with tenderness.

chapters.title: Two Flags, One Wreck
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Verdance and Kestrel Reach council chambers. Both governments dispatch claims teams, each suspecting the other of sabotage. Wren insists Freya is the only pilot both sides will tolerate. Emotional beat: Freya realizing her neutrality is a cage being weaponized.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Cross-referencing the ship's logs with Elena's case file, she finds the missing page referenced in a decades-old research note: temporal decoherence experiments aboard the Halcyon Dawn—Elena's own design. Emotional beat: the ground shifting; her original was both victim and architect.

chapters.title: Children of the Mission
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She bonds with Sef, the ship's reversed engineer, who remembers being old and being Elena's colleague. Sef reveals Elena discovered the colonies' gene-banks were failing and hid the reversal technology to force cooperation. Emotional beat: found family forming in the wreck's cold corridors.

chapters.title: What the Council Raised
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, flashback structure. She recalls her childhood in the Verdance creche—how Wren personally oversaw her cloning, her training, her 'inheritance' of the case. She realizes she was groomed to keep Elena's work buried, not solved. Emotional beat: betrayal reframing her entire life.

chapters.title: Kestrel's Reach
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She risks the forbidden crossing to Kestrel Reach to verify the gene-bank failure herself, guided by a sympathetic dispatcher, Imani. The colony is dying quietly—infertility, decay, denial. Emotional beat: compassion dissolving the border in her mind.

chapters.title: The Message Elena Left
chapters.summary: Freya's POV with Sef's recovered log entries. A hidden recording from Elena: a warning that the reversal process can be reversed again—but only once, and only if both colonies share it. She feared one world would weaponize it. Emotional beat: grief and resolve fusing; Elena trusted no one, but trusted the future.

chapters.title: Wren's Patience
chapters.summary: Aldous Wren's POV. He has managed the Galloway clones for thirty years, waiting for one to find the research so he could control it. He orders Freya's recall, framing it as protection. Emotional beat: cold, paternal menace—the killer's logic laid bare.

chapters.title: Run the Dark Between
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She refuses recall and runs the Halcyon Dawn's engines hot to escape a Verdance interceptor, with the reversed crew as her passengers. Sef, in a child's body, coaxes the old ship through a debris shoal. Emotional beat: the found family becoming a crew, a home in motion.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She decodes the cryo-banks: they hold frozen embryos from both colonies' founding generations—the only viable genetic diversity left. Whoever controls the ship controls humanity's future. Emotional beat: the crushing arithmetic of survival; every choice costs half the sky.

chapters.title: The Interrogation of a Copy
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, intercepted transmission. Wren broadcasts an accusation: clones are property, and Freya has stolen Verdance assets. Both colonies' publics turn on her. Emotional beat: public unmaking—her identity weaponized against her.

chapters.title: Imani's Choice
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. The Kestrel dispatcher must decide whether to shelter the fugitive ship, knowing it could save her dying colony or doom it if Verdance retaliates. She opens the docks. Emotional beat: quiet courage; loyalty chosen over safety.

chapters.title: The Second Reversal
chapters.summary: Freya and Sef's POV. They test Elena's restoration process on one crew member—an old woman's mind returned to an adult body. It works, but the process consumes the cryo-banks' power reserve. Emotional beat: hope with a timer attached.

chapters.title: Council of Ash
chapters.summary: Multi-POV. Wren's faction seizes the Verdance assembly; Kestrel's hawks demand first claim on the embryos. Fleets mobilize toward the Halcyon Dawn's position. Emotional beat: the machinery of war grinding toward the only thing that can save everyone.

chapters.title: Elena's Murder, Solved
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Sef's fragmented memory finally resolves: Wren sabotaged Elena's shuttle after she refused to surrender the research to Verdance alone. Freya broadcasts the evidence to both worlds. Emotional beat: truth as a detonation; loyalty to the dead finally paid.

chapters.title: The Standoff at Dawn's Hull
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Both fleets surround the Halcyon Dawn. Freya, on open channel, offers the impossible deal: the embryos split, the restoration shared, joint custody—or she vents the banks and no one's future survives. Emotional beat: the climax; one clone holding two worlds hostage with their own tomorrow.

chapters.title: Wren's Last Argument
chapters.summary: Freya and Wren's POV, face to face aboard the ship. He argues clones have no standing, that she is Elena's echo making Elena's mistakes. Freya answers with the one thing he never gave her: a self-chosen name. Wren is arrested by his own council when the evidence breaks rank. Emotional beat: identity claimed, not inherited.

chapters.title: What Grows from Shared Ground
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, months later. The first restored crew members work alongside both colonies' scientists; the embryos are thawed under joint charter. Verdance and Kestrel Reach reopen the route—her route. Emotional beat: the long silence ending; a future with room for everyone.

chapters.title: Freya Galloway, Herself
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, final chapter. She files a new registry entry—not Elena's clone, not Wren's creation, but her own name and route. She records one message and, for the first time, sends it. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace; the found family waving her off toward the long route home.
